cards.title: Introduction to Testing
cards.content:
Testing is a crucial part of software development. It ensures your Python code works as expected, prevents regressions, and makes refactoring safer.

Common types of tests include Unit Tests, Integration Tests, and End-to-End Tests.

cards.title: Structure of a Unit Test
cards.content:
Using Python's built-in unittest framework, tests are typically written as classes that inherit from unittest.TestCase.

import unittest

class TestMathOperations(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_addition(self):
        self.assertEqual(1 + 1, 2)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

cards.title: Getting Started with Pytest
cards.content:
pytest is a popular third-party testing framework that makes writing tests cleaner and easier with plain assert statements.

def test_subtract():
    assert 5 - 3 == 2

To run tests, simply execute pytest in your terminal.

items: Pass the fixture name as an argument to the test function
Execute the test function using the fixture setup
Run teardown code after the test completes (if defined using yield)

cards.title: Test-Driven Development (TDD)
cards.content:
TDD is a software development process where you write tests before you write the actual implementation code.

The cycle is often summarized as: Red (write a failing test) -> Green (write code to pass the test) -> Refactor (clean up the code).

items: Write a unit test that fails
Run the test suite to verify the test fails (Red)
Write the minimum amount of production code to pass the test
Run the tests to verify they pass (Green)
Refactor the code while keeping tests green

cards.title: Mocking and Patching
cards.content:
Often your code relies on external APIs, databases, or file systems. You use mocking to replace these parts with dummy objects.

from unittest.mock import patch

@patch('module.requests.get')
def test_api_call(mock_get):
    mock_get.return_value.status_code = 200
    # Test your function that makes an API call

content.question: Why do we use mocks during unit testing?

options.text: To make tests run slower and more accurately
To isolate the code under test from external systems like networks or databases

cards.title: Conclusion and Best Practices
cards.content:
You have learned the essentials of testing in Python using unittest and pytest, alongside concepts like TDD and mocking.

Best Practices: Write tests early, keep them independent, and aim for high code coverage on critical business logic!
